title: Exact attribution gates precede the first Paper-019 H200 diagnostic
abstract: Paper-019 round 2 was killed offline before GPU scoring: canonicalization reduced the 8192-token vocabulary to 6808 keys, but the frozen conservative affected-occurrence mediator was only 3.7155 percent, below the 10 percent gate. Round 1 advanced only in implementation readiness. The FA3 external cumulative-offset contract is now bound to the official Dao-AILab commit and exact vendored artifacts, while local packer generation and speed remain explicitly untested. The default-inert boundary sidecar and its governed runner now implement a 1000-batch exact preclock comparison, a 20-update scanner/scanner checkpoint, a 20-update scanner/sidecar checkpoint, model/optimizer/data/boundary/loss/CPU-RNG/CUDA-RNG hashes, PyTorch-2.9 compile-ID and fail-on-recompile checks, a 10-step washout, and exactly 200 clean timing samples in 20 frozen blocks. Local governance tests pass, but no GPU experiment has launched because setup reconciliation, typed promotion, paper amendment, and adversarial H200 stream/FA3 tests remain open. Independent 2025-2026 proposal and critic agents ranked GPAS and a distinct-prime Engram address chain as strong plateau reserves; these are prospective only. There is no new SOTA, and 0.927183 remains the historical chart origin.
methods: The coordinator registered primary FA3 API provenance from the official NeurIPS paper and exact Dao-AILab source commit, preserving paper/code scope separation and reproducibility hashes. An independent agent ran the frozen canonical-key mediator over the first 64 exact best-fit packed validation rows, with protected-token and alias-provenance checks, and applied the preregistered minimum-across-bigram/trigram rule without post-hoc substitution. Three agents independently implemented, typed, and adversarially audited the boundary-sidecar path. Audit findings were converted into executable failure gates: scheduler-only diagnostic variables, exact singleton markers, phased data and state hashes, runtime compile callbacks, clean timing isolation, fixed block bootstrap, crash-safe invalid pair artifacts, and comparison-only recovery. Two additional independent agents read current 2025-2026 primary literature and separately proposed and criticized a connected plateau reserve. No endpoint or validation score was used to select or tune the sidecar implementation.

findings.statement: The canonicalized-key round is killed before GPU scoring because its frozen strict affected-occurrence mediator is 0.0371551513671875, below 0.10.
limitations: This is an offline addressing mediator, not an endpoint BPB experiment.
The pooled 10.7521 percent and larger alias-exposed shares are diagnostic and cannot replace the prospective minimum-across-orders statistic.

findings.statement: Official FA3 code strongly supports an int32 cumulative-offset varlen API whose offsets are preserved for backward, but it does not support a local OPHIS sidecar speed or efficacy claim.
limitations: The official code snapshot and NeurIPS paper have different temporal versions.
Local packer boundaries, stream lifetimes, charged throughput, and BPB remain untested on H200.

findings.statement: The governed sidecar diagnostic now separates attribution into 20 exact A/A updates, 20 exact A/B updates, a 10-step washout, and 200 clean profile steps, with exact cross-arm state and RNG comparison.
limitations: The implementation is not yet reconciled to the live setup and has not run on H200.
A single physical placement cannot authorize a scored endpoint even if its timing thresholds pass; a counterbalanced profile remains required.

findings.statement: Independent 2025-2026 proposal and critic passes identify GPAS residual activation control and a distinct-prime Engram addressing chain as the strongest connected plateau reserves.
limitations: These are ranked proposals, not registered rounds or measured local effects.
They cannot bypass the current Paper-019 sequence or its five-round paper boundary.

negative_results: Paper-019 round 2 canonicalized keys failed its strict occurrence mediator and will receive no GPU endpoint.
The sidecar cannot advance on a single-placement timing result; the campaign has documented GPU-placement artifacts, so counterbalancing is now an explicit additional requirement.
The current round-3 conditioned-initialization bundle remains mixed: paper-supported Q/K structure and a local disjoint-V extrapolation cannot be conflated.
No GPU launch, adoption, control rebind, chart point, or SOTA claim occurred.
limitations: The local development environment lacks PyTorch, so CUDA/FA3 tests must execute in the pinned remote H200 environment.
The setup reconciliation still points to pre-sidecar train.py and lib.py hashes.
The typed sidecar chain is staged by a helper but has not been applied or promoted into the append-only gated ledger.
Paper 019 must be amended and visually reverified before the strengthened counterbalanced requirement can govern execution.
decisions: Preserve the round-2 mediator kill exactly; do not reinterpret pooled statistics.
Require runtime compile IDs, fail-on-recompile, exact A/A and A/B state/RNG hashes, and 20 clean timing blocks before treating the sidecar diagnostic as valid.
Treat a single-placement threshold pass as requiring a counterbalanced profile, never as direct scored-endpoint authority.
Keep accepted mechanisms cumulative and rejected mechanisms comparator-inert.
Retain 0.927183 only as the historical chart anchor and retain the no-new-SOTA verdict.

next_hour_plan.question: Do adversarial H200 tests prove delayed H2D, delayed consumer, ring wrap, wrong-stream rejection, poisoned-tail isolation, and actual FA3 forward/backward parity?
next_hour_plan.why_now: The one-shot governed diagnostic must not be spent on a race or recompilation bug that a focused systems test could expose.
next_hour_plan.stop_condition: Do not launch on any CUDA error, stale lease, overwritten slot, incorrect logical prefix, state/gradient mismatch, second Dynamo compile ID, or missing negative-control failure.

next_hour_plan.question: Can the strengthened sidecar protocol be frozen into the ICML paper, typed chain, setup reconciliation, challenge selection, and warning-free strict audit?
next_hour_plan.why_now: The implementation and execution authority must describe the same causal question before remote mutation.
next_hour_plan.stop_condition: Stop on any stale hash, untyped dependency, score mismatch, non-singleton marker, unresolved audit finding, or paper/render discrepancy.

next_hour_plan.question: Does the governed pair preserve every exact A/A and A/B hash and show a single-placement token-rate ratio above 1.054 with 95 percent LCB above 1.041?
next_hour_plan.why_now: A valid negative result kills a low-plausibility systems idea cheaply; a positive result only justifies the separately frozen counterbalanced profile.
next_hour_plan.stop_condition: Kill on any semantic mismatch, compile/recompile failure, co-tenancy, fewer than 20 clean blocks, point-ratio miss, or LCB miss.

next_hour_plan.question: Can the next paper replace the dead canonical-key round with a distinct-prime-modulus Engram assay without changing parameter count or bundling later memory mechanisms?
next_hour_plan.why_now: Both independent critic and local code comparison identify structured shared power-of-two collisions as a more direct, source-faithful address mechanism.
next_hour_plan.stop_condition: Do not promote if frozen tuple collision, joint-collision dependence, occupancy entropy, or parameter-count mediators show no material improvement.
